# Real Angular build fixtures

Captured on Linux on 2026-10-02 using Angular CLI/framework/build 22.2.1,
TypeScript 6.0.3, Node 24.19.0, and npm 11.9.0. Each `.stdout.txt` and
`.stderr.txt` is an unmodified capture from the same `ng build` process with
`CI=1 NG_CLI_ANALYTICS=false`, non-TTY streams and default progress enabled.
The command resolved the installed local CLI via `node_modules/.bin` on PATH.
Absolute source/output paths, timestamps and durations are deliberately intact.
`help.txt` is the actual `ng build --help` output used for the argument grammar.

The app was generated by the official `@angular/cli@22.2.1` with
`ng new fixture-app --routing --style=css --skip-git --skip-install --defaults`.
Packages came from the official npm registry with lifecycle scripts disabled.
The generated welcome page was replaced with a small local-only header, text,
router outlet and system-font CSS. No remote assets were fetched by the builds.

- `success`: normal production build, exit 0
- `lazy-chunks`: six ordinary dashboard/projects/reports/settings/help/profile
  routes, each loading a standalone component, exit 0
- `budget-warning`: initial maximumWarning `100kB`, maximumError `1MB`, exit 0
- `budget-error`: initial maximumWarning `100kB`, maximumError `150kB`, exit 1
- `typescript-error`: number-typed property assigned `'not-a-number'`, exit 1
- `template-error`: nonexistent `missingTitle()` referenced by the template,
  with both template and component source context, exit 1

The filter removes no bundle rows, sizes, warnings, errors or context. Default
and six-route success fixtures exceed 20% reduction using RTK's production
bytes/4 token estimator, mainly from table padding and redundant progress.
Diagnostic-heavy builds save less; compiler-error-only output is unchanged.
These figures are output estimates, not billing or real-tokenizer measurements.
